overview: From 2026-11-18 to 2026-11-19, ethereum-optimism/optimism had 16 new PRs (24 merged), 10 new issues, and 34 active contributors.

topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: prepare the cutover
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
The cutover (#20266) should hold only what needs the `go.mod` change. This issue collects the work that can land before it.

## Why now

The ratchet [type-checks the tree against go-ethereum v1.17.2](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/8c35adb181f5192cb5db19499ee2f7ea2731fcce/ops/scripts/opgeth-ratchet/upstream.go#L30-L40), the version op-geth is based on. The cutover moves to the latest release, v1.17.10. A trial run of the ratchet against each of v1.17.7 to v1.17.10 gives the same result:

- The "upstream backport" entries of the [allowlist](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/8c35adb181f5192cb5db19499ee2f7ea2731fcce/ops/scripts/opgeth-ratchet/allowlist.txt) are no longer needed.
- More APIs differ, and the allowlist shows none of them:
  - changed signatures: `core.IntrinsicGas`, `core.FloorDataGas`, `core.ApplyTransaction`, `core.ProcessBeaconBlockRoot`, `core.ProcessParentBlockHash`, `state.StateDB.Commit`, `IntermediateRoot` and `SetTxContext`, `vm.EVM.Call` and `Create`, `node.NewHTTPHandlerStack`
  - missing symbols: `params.BlobScheduleConfig.Osaka` and `.Amsterdam`, `params.DefaultOsakaBlobConfig`, `core.GasPool.Gas`, `core.ErrInsufficientBalanceWitness`
  - `engine.ExecutableData.BlockAccessList` is a `[]byte` upstream
- Production code is affected in `op-batcher/batcher`, `op-service/rpc` and `op-service/txinclude`. The rest is tests and test support.

The tree has also never run its tests against upstream go-ethereum.

## Work

- [x] Make the ratchet type-check against the cutover version, and list the API differences above as cutover edits.
- [ ] Shed the OP fork fields and the `Optimism` struct from `op-core/params.GethChainConfig()`. After #24156, `GethChainConfig()` and `GethGenesis()` have no caller outside `op-core/params` and `op-core/genesis` except tests. This settles the audit item of #20266.
- [ ] Pin golden vectors for the values that only the op-geth differential tests pin today, e.g. user deposits with a mint, a value or a contract creation.
- [ ] Delete the op-geth differential tests, as the last PR before the cutover.
- [ ] Stop using a differing API where the code can do without it, e.g. `core.ErrInsufficientBalanceWitness`.
- [ ] Open the cutover PR as a draft and run CI on it. Move every fix that does not need the `go.mod` change into a PR of its own.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5.2*

topIssues.title: kona-disc: Save only proven ENRs in the bootstore
topIssues.author: aakoshh
topIssues.body:
kona-node's bootstore saves ENRs that nobody has verified, and dials every one of them at the next startup. A peer answering our lookups with freshly generated records can push the honest ones out and eclipse the node after a restart. Records that point at a third party's address make every kona node that saves them dial it at each restart. Found while working on #23715.

### Current behaviour
- **Saved without proof.** The discovery driver saves records from `Discovered`, `SessionEstablished` and `UnverifiableEnr` ([driver.rs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1ee89a21d9304d4cfea6e39ab407e3b689f115b9/rust/kona/crates/node/disc/src/driver.rs#L318-L350)), and every 60 s writes them all to `bootstore.json`. What each event proves:
  - `Discovered` fires for every record in a NODES response, before any check. discv5 documents these as "not guaranteed to be live or contactable", and the only check is the record's own signature.
  - `SessionEstablished` proves the UDP endpoint, but not the TCP port gossip dials.
  - `UnverifiableEnr` means discv5 found that the record doesn't match where the node's packets come from. discv5 even removes such a node from its table; kona saves it and dials it.
- **All dialed at startup.** Every stored record for the chain is forwarded to the gossip dialer ([driver.rs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1ee89a21d9304d4cfea6e39ab407e3b689f115b9/rust/kona/crates/node/disc/src/driver.rs#L213-L220)), up to 2048 of them. The redial limit is kept in memory, so it starts from zero after every restart.
- **Never removed.** The only way out is rotation, once the store holds more than 2048 records ([store.rs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1ee89a21d9304d4cfea6e39ab407e3b689f115b9/rust/kona/crates/node/peers/src/store.rs#L195-L208)). Duplicates are detected by comparing whole records, so a node's corrected record (higher `seq`) is stored next to its stale one, and both are dialed. Records that fail to connect are never removed.
- The store is only used as a list of addresses to dial. `bootstrap_peers` puts only the hard-coded bootnodes into the discv5 table, so discovery itself recovers from them, but the first gossip peers after a restart come from the store.

### What op-node does
geth's node database starts discovery only from nodes that answered our PING from that IP within the last 5 days, at most 30 of them (`QuerySeeds(seedCount, seedMaxAge)` in `p2p/discover/table.go`). They go into the discovery table to be checked again; they aren't dialed directly. Since 1.8, a node must also stay in the table for 5 minutes before it's saved. [Low-Resource Eclipse Attacks on Ethereum's Peer-to-Peer Network](https://eprint.iacr.org/2018/236) (2018) describes eclipsing geth through its database and table with two hosts; geth's rules are the result.

### Proposal
- **Save only proven records:**
  - Save a record only after an outbound libp2p connection to it succeeds with the matching peer ID. That's the only proof that its TCP address reaches a node holding the key. Dialing lookup results while running stays as it is.
  - `NodeInserted` isn't enough. It proves the UDP endpoint, not the TCP port. Inbound sessions also trigger it, so without discv5's `ip_limit` (#23764) one IP with many keys can produce as many as it likes.
- **Unverifiable records:** neither save nor dial them. Count them in metrics.
- **Cleanup:**
  - Keep one record per node ID, the one with the highest `seq`.
  - Apply a per-subnet limit to stored records (the paper's Countermeasure 2 applied to the stored database).
  - Keep the set dialed at startup small, preferring records proven recently.
  - Drop records whose dials keep failing.
  - Run the address-scope check (#23766) on records loaded at startup, which clears records saved before this change.

### Tests
- A `Discovered` record is saved only after a gossip connection to it succeeds. A record whose dial fails, or reaches a different peer ID, is never saved.
- An `UnverifiableEnr` record is neither saved nor dialed.
- The bootstore keeps only the newest record per node ID, and no more than the per-subnet limit from one /24.
- Flooding the node with fresh-key records for our chain doesn't push proven records out.
- Startup dials at most the configured number of stored records, and drops stored records that fail the scope check.

topIssues.title: kona-node: Don't serve the P2P control methods to anyone who can reach the RPC port
topIssues.author: aakoshh
topIssues.body:
kona-node serves the `opp2p_*` methods to anyone who can reach its RPC port, and listens on all interfaces by default. Several of those methods change the node's peering: a caller can cut the node off from every peer. Found while working on #23715.

### Current behaviour
- `--rpc.addr` defaults to `0.0.0.0` (`rust/kona/bin/node/src/flags/rpc.rs`). Its doc says privileged methods aren't exposed by it alone, but that's only true of `admin`.
- The P2P API is always merged into the RPC server (`rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/service/node/rollup.rs`). Only the `admin` namespace is behind `--rpc.enable-admin`.
- Since #23715, the methods are stronger than before:
  - `opp2p_blockSubnet 0.0.0.0/0` (and `::/0`) closes every connection, including static and protected peers, and refuses all new ones. Before, a block only stopped the node's own dials.
  - `opp2p_unblockPeer` also lifts score bans.
  - `opp2p_connectPeer` returns the dial's error, which names each address and its I/O error ("Connection refused", a timeout, "Unexpected peer ID"). That lets a caller probe which hosts and ports the node can reach. For a `/dns*` address, it also resolves the name on the network actor's thread.
- op-node is the same: it also defaults `rpc.addr` to `0.0.0.0` (`op-node/flags/flags.go`), and registers the P2P API whenever P2P is on, with only `admin` behind `EnableAdmin` (`op-node/node/node.go`). Operators are expected to keep the RPC port private.

### Proposal
- Serve the methods that change peering (`blockPeer`, `unblockPeer`, `blockAddr`, `unblockAddr`, `blockSubnet`, `unblockSubnet`, `protectPeer`, `unprotectPeer`, `connectPeer`, `disconnectPeer`) only with `--rpc.enable-admin`, or behind authentication. This diverges from op-node, so it needs agreeing with the op-node side, or a kona-only flag.
- Or default `--rpc.addr` to `127.0.0.1`, which also diverges from op-node.
- Either way, correct the `--rpc.addr` doc, and document in `docs/public-docs/node-operators/kona-node/rpc/p2p.mdx` that the P2P API must not be exposed publicly.
- Consider returning a generic dial-failure message over RPC and logging the full error, and resolving DNS names off the network actor.

topIssues.title: op-reth, kona: cover the historical fork-boundary execution rules that op-e2e/opgeth tested
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
[`op-e2e/opgeth/op_geth_test.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/72fcf9479ea7ee1105b823d23da8bf58ba58136d/op-e2e/opgeth/op_geth_test.go) drove op-geth through the Engine API with hand-built payload attributes to pin fork-boundary execution rules. The package is deleted with the in-process op-geth engine (#20275, #23864). Most of its cases have an op-reth-side equivalent in op-revm / op-reth unit tests, the kona proof tests on `op-reth-test-engine`, or the action tests. A review of #23864 found no op-reth equivalent for the cases below. The list comes from a search, not from an exhaustive audit, so confirm each gap before writing a test.

| op-geth test | Rule | Closest existing coverage |
|---|---|---|
| [`TestPreregolith` UnusedGasConsumed](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/72fcf9479ea7ee1105b823d23da8bf58ba58136d/op-e2e/opgeth/op_geth_test.go#L358), [`TestRegolith` ReturnUnusedGasToPool](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/72fcf9479ea7ee1105b823d23da8bf58ba58136d/op-e2e/opgeth/op_geth_test.go#L547) | Pre-Regolith a deposit consumes its whole gas limit from the block gas pool; from Regolith on, unused gas returns to the pool | none found (rule in `alloy-op-evm`'s block executor) |
| [`TestPreCanyon`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/72fcf9479ea7ee1105b823d23da8bf58ba58136d/op-e2e/opgeth/op_geth_test.go#L734) | Blocks have nil withdrawals before Canyon; `PUSH0` is rejected | none found |
| [`TestPreEcotone`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/72fcf9479ea7ee1105b823d23da8bf58ba58136d/op-e2e/opgeth/op_geth_test.go#L868), [`TestEcotone`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/72fcf9479ea7ee1105b823d23da8bf58ba58136d/op-e2e/opgeth/op_geth_test.go#L934) | `TSTORE` is rejected before Ecotone and accepted after | only the spec-id mapping in `op-revm` |
| [`TestPreFjord`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/72fcf9479ea7ee1105b823d23da8bf58ba58136d/op-e2e/opgeth/op_geth_test.go#L1012) | The P256VERIFY precompile is absent before Fjord | post-Fjord presence is covered by the Fjord acceptance checks |
| [`TestInvalidDepositInFCU`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/72fcf9479ea7ee1105b823d23da8bf58ba58136d/op-e2e/opgeth/op_geth_test.go#L85), [`TestMissingGasLimit`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/72fcf9479ea7ee1105b823d23da8bf58ba58136d/op-e2e/opgeth/op_geth_test.go#L41) | A failing deposit in payload attributes still yields a block; attributes without a gas limit are rejected | unit tests only, no Engine API block build |

Every live OP Stack chain is past these forks, so the value of each case is in guarding the historical-sync path of op-reth and kona. The natural home is the kona proof / action tests on `op-reth-test-engine`, which already build blocks from payload attributes at a chosen fork (see `TestDepositGasParity`). Decide per row whether to add a case there or record that the rule is covered well enough upstream (opcode gating lives in upstream revm).

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5.2*

topIssues.title: op-supernode: Stop with an error when an interop DB fails to open
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
If op-supernode cannot open its interop DBs at start-up, it starts without cross-chain checks.

`interop.New` logs an error and returns nil when the verified DB or a logs DB fails to open (`op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/interop.go:264-282`). The supernode then skips the interop activity and registers no verifier (`op-supernode/supernode/supernode.go:141-145`). Without a verifier, `FullyVerifiedL2Head` and `FinalizedL2Head` return `VerifierHeadPreActivation` (`chain_container/super_authority.go`). Safe and finalized heads then follow local-safe with no interop check, and proxyd-cl followers can adopt them.

`superroot` still gets a typed nil `*Interop` as its verified reader (`supernode.go:129-130`). `superroot_atTimestamp` then dereferences nil in `VerifiedResultAtTimestamp`.

op-supernode should stop with an error when an interop DB fails to open and interop is configured.

Found in the review of the Combined Lagoon Interop FMA. Filed by Claude.

topPRs.title: docs/public-docs: run the docs preview and tooling on mise-pinned bun
topPRs.author: pauldowman
topPRs.body:
Previewing docs.optimism.io locally needed Node, pnpm and a globally installed `mint` CLI, none of which the repo pins. The documented `pnpm dev` failed out of the box, and `pnpm install` itself failed under the pinned pnpm because of a placeholder `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. `just public-docs` now installs dependencies and serves the preview using only the `bun` and `just` pinned in `mise.toml`, and the generators and lints run on the same `bun`.

- **Effect on contributors:** `pnpm …` commands become `bun run …`, and Node, pnpm and tsx are no longer needed. No effect on the published site: Mintlify deploys through its GitHub app and doesn't run `package.json` scripts, and no CI job installs the docs' JS dependencies.
- **`mint` is an exact-pinned devDependency** of `docs/public-docs`, so `bun.lock` locks its whole dependency tree, rather than pinning a `bunx mint@<version>` call in the root justfile.
- **More advisories become visible; the risk is not new.** `bun audit` on the docs package goes from 8 to 43 advisories, almost all in versions that `mint` pins exactly. Contributors already ran these same packages through a global `mint` install or `npx`; the repo just had no record of them, so nothing could flag them. Exposure is a localhost preview, and the fix is bumping `mint`, which Renovate can now see (expect frequent `mint` bump PRs). `sharp` is overridden to 0.35.5 because `mint` pins the vulnerable 0.33.5, restoring the protection #22733 added.
- **`react`/`react-dom` removed:** they were unused (Mintlify supplies React at runtime; `components/HomeCard.tsx` only imports types), and their React 18 was loaded instead of `mint`'s React 19, which crashed `mint dev`.
- **Accepted:** the existing `minimatch >=9.0.7` override forces minimatch 10 onto Spectral, a `mint` dependency expecting ^3. Spectral only reaches that code for rulesets with `overrides`, and this site has no OpenAPI or AsyncAPI specs.
- Tutorials that tell readers to use pnpm, npx or tsx for their own projects are unchanged.
- `lint:nav` (887 errors) and `lint:reference` (3 errors) fail identically on `develop`; not addressed here.

Reviews: `ci-config-reviewer` and `deletion-reviewer` ran on the branch; their findings are fixed. `/op:security-reviewer` has not run yet and must run before this is marked ready. Unconfirmed: whether GitHub's dependency graph and the `dependency-review` check parse `bun.lock`.

topPRs.title: kona-peers,kona-disc,kona-gossip!: Keep confirmed peers in the bootstore
topPRs.author: aakoshh
topPRs.body:
### What

The bootstore records how each saved peer was confirmed, and a full store keeps the confirmed ones. Second PR of a stack for #23767, on top of #24155.

For operators:
- The file is `{"version": 1, "records": [...]}`, one record per node, with `udp_verified_at` (a discovery session that lasted five minutes) and `tcp_verified_at` (gossip dialed the node at its record's TCP address). Old files, a plain list, are read and rewritten.
- A full store evicts unconfirmed records first and peers gossip reached last, so sessions under fresh keys no longer push out peers that work.
- A public-only node no longer dials back a private node that started a session with it; the private node dials, and can redial. `kona_node_discovery_events{type="session_established"}` no longer counts those sessions.
- Saved records without a TCP address are no longer handed to gossip, which counted a dial error for each every minute.

BREAKING CHANGE: the bootstore file format changes; earlier kona-node versions fail on it at startup, so delete the file to go back. In kona-peers, `BootStore::open` returns only the store, `SkippedEntry` and `SkipReason` are gone, `valid_peers_with_chain_id` returns an iterator, and `BootStoreError` has a `NewerVersion` variant.

### Why

The bootstore saved every session's record, with nothing to tell a peer that worked from one that never did, and evicted the oldest when full. Anyone starting sessions under fresh keys could replace every saved peer, so that after a restart the node would bootstrap from the attacker's records.

### How

- Evidence is only what the node saw itself. A session counts once discv5 still holds it after five minutes, which means it answered a ping, much as geth saves a node only after several. A connection counts only if we dialed it: op-node dials from its listen port, so an inbound connection can come from the record's address without showing that we can reach it.
- Among unconfirmed sessions, the youngest is evicted first, as the attacker picks the rate of fresh ones. Ties are broken at random, not by node ID, which keys can be ground for.
- Dialing back without saving, from #23766, is reverted: a node that dials a record it doesn't save can never redial it, and its dial can leave the other node with only an inbound connection, which confirms nothing.

### Caveats

- The per-/24 limit on the store is deferred to #23764: one host with many keys can still fill it with records whose addresses work.
- Evidence uses wall-clock time, so a large clock jump can count a fresh session as lasted.
- Evidence doesn't expire yet; that's a later PR.

### Alternatives

- An invalid entry is skipped with `serde_with::VecSkipError` and logged with serde's error, rather than parsed entry by entry to log its content.
- Review agents run: `rust-code-reviewer` and `deletion-reviewer`; each fix has its own commit. Dismissed: the invalid-entry WARN not naming the file or the entry, moving gossip's private `tcp_socket` to kona-peers, and the Korean configuration page, left to the translation PRs. The general code review and security review skills weren't run.

### Potential follow-ups

- Seed discovery from the stored records, and hand gossip only confirmed ones (next PR).
- Expire evidence, once discovery has heard from the network after a restart.

🤖 Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5

topPRs.title: op-core,op-chain-ops,op-node: pin golden vectors for the values only op-geth pins
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
The op-geth differential tests are deleted at the cutover to upstream go-ethereum, and some op-core values lose their only pin with them. This pins those values as golden vectors while op-geth is still there to prove them. Test files only.

Every literal is op-geth's output, and this PR's CI proves it: the existing differential tests now run over the same case tables as the golden tests, or a new assertion compares op-geth's output with the literal. The op-geth half goes with the differential tests; the tables and literal assertions stay, and the files that stay use nothing that only op-geth provides.

Pinned:
- **Deposit transactions:** binary encoding, hash and JSON for nil mint, nil value, empty data, the system-tx flag and extreme values; JSON with a nonce and without the `isSystemTx` key.
- **Receipts:** trie preimage, binary and RLP encodings of deposit receipts before Regolith, before Canyon and after it, with and without logs; a post-exec receipt; the receipts root over a mixed list.
- **Fees:** `L1CostBedrock`, `L1CostFjord` (including a zero FastLZ size and large sizes with maximal scalars), and `TxRollupCostData` per transaction type, unsigned and signed.
- **DA footprint:** the constants, every error path of the scalar extraction, and the footprint for the transaction-type mix, extra deposits and boundary scalars.
- **Chain config and genesis:** the exact chain-config JSON (key set and order), decoding op-geth-written configs and genesis files with and without `osakaTime`, the genesis header hash per fork schedule and message-passer variant, the full genesis JSON, and `NewL2Genesis` per schedule.
- **Other encodings:** post-exec transaction JSON, receipt JSON including `l1FeeScalar`, and the span-batch fields of a post-exec transaction.

`TestFjordL1CostParity` now runs over the golden table instead of its previous parameter grid.

Stacked on #24184, whose `CalcDAFootprint` takes binary-encoded transactions: the DA footprint vectors hold deposits, which a go-ethereum transaction cannot hold after the cutover.

Part of #24172.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.2*

topPRs.title: op-zk-proposer: extend and defend only the anchor and its own games
topPRs.author: digorithm
topPRs.body:
The proposer adopted the highest valid game as its parent whoever created it, and defended, resolved and closed any game whose prestate it could load. Every foreign ancestor puts the games we build on it at risk, and third parties control how many exist and how long they span (audit findings 3, 5 and 11; also the unsafe-L1-head game that is challenged at the last minute). After this PR the proposer extends only the anchor or games it owns, and defends only games it owns. This reverses the position in #22111, agreed with @pauldowman and Gustavo after the audit.

Effect on operators:
- A game is owned when its creator is the signer or listed in the new `OP_ZK_PROPOSER_OWNED_CREATORS`, and its prestate is known. Set the variable to the old signer when rotating the key, and remove it once the anchor has moved past the old signer's last game. Unset is the normal state.
- Upgrade step: this version no longer defends foreign games, including a foreign parent of an in-flight signer game. Before deploying, check that no in-progress signer game has an unresolved foreign ancestor; if one does, list that creator in `OP_ZK_PROPOSER_OWNED_CREATORS` until the anchor has moved past it.
- The span of games built on the head is now capped. While the proposer keeps up, a game spans one proposal interval. When it falls two or more intervals behind (downtime, or games that take longer than an interval to create or, in fast finality mode, to prove), a game spans up to the new `OP_ZK_PROPOSER_MAX_PROPOSAL_SPAN_INTERVALS` intervals (default 4). Before this PR the catch-up game spanned the whole gap. Bond and prove duration must cover the configured maximum.
- `OP_ZK_PROPOSER_PROPOSAL_INTERVAL_SECONDS=0` now fails at startup. It used to mean "propose at the safe head".
- Foreign games are no longer resolved or closed by the proposer. op-challenger or their creator does it. Until then, `op_dispute_mon_zk_games_pending_lifecycle_action` counts them, and an owned game created on a foreign parent before this change cannot resolve. Claims stay credit-driven, so challenger bonds already earned on foreign games are still claimed.
- The info log "Discovered game created by another proposer" is gone.

Reasons the diff does not show:
- Foreign games stay cached as untrusted records because tracking the anchor needs their factory index; without them an anchor move to a foreign game rescans the factory.
- Head selection follows a chain down to the anchor, a root, or an owned game that resolved `DefenderWins` (its ancestors can no longer lose). Anyone can move the anchor to a valid foreign game; without the `DefenderWins` stop, a restart that leaves our chain's root outside the discovery window made the whole chain fail the check.
- On a UUID collision with a foreign root while the anchor is not a ZK game, the proposer now walks one second like on the normal path instead of waiting for the next interval. The wait relied on the foreign root becoming our head; without that, one copy per interval would stop creation.
- When the registry rejects the head's chain, the fallback root keeps the head's timestamp and can span more than one interval. Recomputing it from the anchor livelocks. With no anchor game registered, a broken chain likewise restarts from the last head's timestamp.

Accepted risk (security review finding): a UUID does not include the creator, so a third party can create our next game first. The proposer walks one second and retries, so stopping creation takes a copy of every attempt, each with a bond that comes back to the attacker (unchallenged, or self-challenged). The README states this. A follow-up tracks a fix.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/proofs-team/issues/48

Review findings dismissed or deferred:
- Make `proposal_interval_seconds` a `NonZeroU64`: `from_env`, the only production constructor, rejects zero, and devstack already does.
- Replace the candidate tuples with a struct: the tuple shape predates this PR.
- A creation guard whose game never reaches the cache (a create dropped by a reorg deeper than the 3-confirmation receipt wait and never mined again) can stop creation until a restart. If the dropped game spanned one interval, the bounded catch-up plans past it once the proposer is two intervals behind. If it was a full-span catch-up game, the next plan never exceeds the guarded timestamp, so creation stops until a restart. Deferred to a follow-up issue.
- The registry-rejection fallback can still skip a root that would not advance a new registry's anchor root, if that root is at or above head plus the maximum span. This needs a registry whose starting root is ahead of our newest proposal.
- No acceptance test asserts the prover-credit claim after defending a listed creator's game; the scenario test `foreign_game_proven_by_the_signer_is_claimed_after_a_third_party_resolves_it` covers the claim path.

The ZK acceptance suite was not run locally; it runs in CI. `kona-sp1-cost-reviewer` does not apply because no guest code changes.

topPRs.title: kona-peers,kona-disc: Seed from and expire the bootstore
topPRs.author: aakoshh
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #24217. Closes #23767.

### What

After a restart, kona-node finds its peers by seeding discovery with the bootstore's records, rather than having gossip dial every saved record every minute. The bootstore forgets the peers it can no longer confirm.

For operators:
- Up to 30 saved records seed discovery at startup, at random, with the peers the node dialed in the last week first. While discovery has fewer than 30 peers connected, 30 others replace those that didn't answer, every minute.
- Gossip redials a peer it dialed since startup and lost, every minute for a day. It no longer dials the peers saved before a restart, or records that only a discovery session confirmed.
- The bootnodes are dialed once at startup. A node that runs gossip without discovery is better listed in `--p2p.static-peers`.
- A record whose address wasn't confirmed for a week is dropped, and one never confirmed an hour or two after its last session. Expiry runs only an hour after a session, so a node without network access keeps its store.
- After the upgrade, the records saved by earlier versions have no evidence, and those that don't answer are dropped about an hour after the first session.

### Why

#24217 records which saved peers are proven, but nothing used it. Gossip redialed every saved record every minute, including those of a flood of sessions under fresh keys, and the store kept every record until it was full.

### How

- The durations are discovery's: the driver passes them to the store (`BootStore::expire(now, ttl)`, and a grace on `session_started`). `valid_peers_with_chain_id` returns entries, so that callers can see the evidence.
- Reseeding removes only the driver's own seeds that are still disconnected: discv5 adds a seed as disconnected, which it refuses into a full bucket.
- The numbers follow geth (30 seeds, random among the proven, expiry hourly once a session showed the network works) and op-node (a day for a discovered address, a week for static peers).

### Caveats

- A host that sleeps, or a clock that jumps forward, by more than a week makes the next pass expire with the jumped clock. Detecting it needs a monotonic clock next to the wall clock: see #24226.
- Any handshake opens the expiry gate, as in geth.
- A node that settles below 30 connected discovery peers keeps drawing seeds every minute. It removes only its own seeds that didn't answer.
- Many identities on one host can still fill the first tier: the per-/24 limit is #23764, connection limits #23700.

### Alternatives

- Seeding the most recently confirmed peers first: those are the peers connected at shutdown, so an eclipse then would seed itself again. For the same reason, the peers reached before a restart aren't redialed.
- A 24 h TTL, as geth: a node stopped for more than a day would lose the ranking of every peer it reached.
- Review: rust-code-reviewer and a security review ran. deletion-reviewer was skipped: no public name, metric, flag or config key is removed.

### Potential follow-ups

- A counter of the session records discovery doesn't dial, by reason.
- Keep the records not yet tried since a long downtime from expiring, as Bitcoin's addrman does.
